 I am new to using stan but have been reading through other people's posts about an error message that am also  getting when I run the code below. Unfortanatelly, I have failed to fix the problem myself. In the code, I am trying to fit a joint model to a longitudinal outcome (y1), a binary outcome (y2)  and survival  outcome (survt), which is not observed directly. I am therefore treating it as a trasformed parameter because it involved parameters "delta" and random effects "b[, 4]. I am trying to fitt a piecewise exponetial  for the  survival component. Any help  to fix the error message "  stan::math::poisson_log: Rate parameter is -73.6109, but must be >= 0!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine, but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."   will be highly appreciated.
 
Thanks in advance,
 
Olive
 
 data{
int<lower=1> Nobs; // number of observations
real time[Nobs];
real y1[Nobs];
int<lower=-3> K;
int<lower=0> N; // number of subjects
int<lower=1,upper=N> id[Nobs]; // subject ID
real time2[N];
int<lower=0,upper=1>  y2[N];
int<lower=0,upper=1>  fail[N];
vector[4] zero; // a vector of zeros
int<lower=0> T;
real g;
real q;
}
parameters{
real delta; // fixeffs
vector[3] beta;// fixeffs
real alpha;// fixeffs
vector[3] gama;// fixeffs
vector[3] r;// fixeffs
vector[4] b[N]; // subj raneffs
real b5[N]; // subj raneffs
real<lower=0> sigma_e; // residual variance
vector<lower=0>[4] sigma_b; // subj variance
corr_matrix[4] Omega_b; // corr matrix for
// subj raneffs
vector<lower=0>[4] h0; // hazard for each interval

}
transformed parameters{
cov_matrix[4] Sigma_b; // varcov matrix for subj ranefs
real survt[N]; // survival time
for (j in 1:N){
survt[j] <- time2[j]-(delta + b[id[j],4]);
}
 
for(l in 1:4){
for(c in 1:4){
Sigma_b[l,c] <- sigma_b[l] * sigma_b[c] * Omega_b[l,c];
}
}
}

model{
real mu[Nobs];
real A[Nobs];
int idt[N,T]; 
int dN[N,T];
vector[T] D[N];

real  t[T+1];
real  maximum ;
for(i in 1:Nobs){
A[i] <- time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4]);
mu[i] <-K;
if (A[i]==0){
mu[i] <- mu[i]; 
} else if (A[i]>0){
mu[i] <- mu[i] + beta[1]*(time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4])) + beta[2]*((time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4]))*(time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4]))) + b[id[i],1]*(time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4]))+ b[id[i],2]*((time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4]))*(time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4])));
}
else{
mu[i] <- mu[i] + beta[3]*(time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4])) + b[id[i],3]*(time[i]-(delta + b[id[i],4]));
}  
}
y1 ~ normal(mu,sigma_e);
b ~ multi_normal(zero,Sigma_b);
 maximum<-max(survt);
 t[1]<-0;
 t[2]<-maximum/4;
 t[3]<-(maximum/4)*2;
 t[4]<-(maximum/4)*3;
 t[5]<- maximum/4;
for (j in 1:N){
 for (i in 1:T){
    dN[j,i]<- int_step(survt[j]-t[i])*fail[j]*int_step(t[i+1]-survt[j]);
   D[j,i]<-(fmin(survt[j], t[i+1])-t[i])*int_step(survt[j]-t[i]);
   }
 
}
 
for (j in 1:N){
 for (i in 1:T){
h0[i]~ gamma(q*g, g);
   //if (D[j,i]!=0)
 increment_log_prob(poisson_log(dN[j,i], h0[i]*D[j,i]*exp(gama[1]*b[id[j],1]+ gama[2]*b[id[j],2]+gama[3]*b[id[j],3])));
  }
}
 
for(j in 1:N){
y2 ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha + r[1]*b[id[j],1]+ r[2]*b[id[j],2]+r[3]*b[id[j],3]);
}
 
sigma_b ~ gamma(1.5,1.0E-4);
sigma_e ~ gamma(1.5,1.0E-4);
Omega_b ~ lkj_corr(2.0);
delta ~ normal(0, 100);
gama ~ normal(0, 100);
}
